item.title: 'You're not welcome here' - Chelsea's Fofana booed by own fans
item.description: Wesley Fofana has made 10 appearances for Chelsea this season. [Getty Images] Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana was subjected to repeated boos and told "you're not welcome here" by his own fans during Friday's Premier League defeat by Nottingham Forest. The jeers aimed at the 25-year-old were heard every time he touched the ball and came after an unauthorised interview with French YouTuber Zach Nani was released. In that controversial two-hour conversation, Fofana also appeared to joke about missing his penalty during last month's Carabao Cup shootout defeat by Liverpool. Manager Xabi Alonso said the French centre-back had apologised and "it won't be repeated". But Fofana endured a difficult time in his side's trip to Forest as supporters made their feelings known. After Chelsea went behind to a brilliant volley from Igor Jesus in the fifth minute, Fofana also conceded a penalty for the home side's second goal from Morgan Gibbs-White in the 51st minute. He was booked for the foul on Liam Delap in the box, and then replaced by Levi Colwill in the 56th minute - just after Emmanuel Emegha had pulled a goal back for the visitors - before Gibbs-White made it 3-1 in the 72nd minute. Emegha scored again in the 89th minute to make it 3-2, but Forest held on to secure their first win over Chelsea at the City Ground since 1997. Meanwhile, Nani has moved to defend Fofana, saying the player was "clearly" not happy during the interview and admitted he had to perform better. Fofana also explained he opted to take a penalty against Liverpool as one of the senior players on the pitch, having joined in a £75m move from Leicester City in 2022. But he confessed football had reached a stage where he was "more unhappy than happy", before recovering physically and mentally. The release of the interview has coincided with the club's poor run of form, with Chelsea losing 4-1 at home to Leeds United last weekend to make it three defeats in four matches. The defence, in particular, has come in for criticism, with the Blues one of four clubs to have conceded more than 20 goals in the Premier League after 11 matches. Having been subjected to racist abuse in the past, Fofana spoke about handling comments during a club-organised interview on this summer's pre-season tour of Asia. He is understood to be one of the highest earners at Stamford Bridge. Fofana has apologised for interview - Alonso Interviewer defends Fofana after backlash

item.title: DK Metcalf’s sign language celebration explained as he sends Aaron Rodgers message
item.description: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images DK Metcalf responded in style following a difficult past week for him with a touchdown in the opening quarter against the Denver Broncos. The Pittsburgh Steelers had to return their attention to the on-field action after what has been an incredible past few days for the franchise. Wide receiver Metcalf headed into the game on Friday without his usual quarterback, Aaron Rodgers. Metcalf had only scored two touchdowns this year prior to the game against Denver, with his first-quarter score seeing him pull out an impressive sign language celebration. What DK Metcalf’s sign language celebration actually meant This is not the first time Metcalf has used this celebration in the NFL. The wideout has previously pulled a similar celebration out during his stint with the Seattle Seahawks. However, there will be very few fans who will have known the exact meaning behind it. Reporter Arye Pulli claimed Metcalf said, “Stand on business, 8″. Rodgers, of course, was number eight for the Steelers, with Metcalf seemingly showing his support for the former quarterback. Despite struggling to show it on the field, Rodgers and Metcalf had formed a strong connection since they both landed in Pittsburgh. It is a telling statement of where Metcalf’s loyalties lie when it comes to the ongoing saga between Mike McCarthy and Rodgers. As for Metcalf, it is about time he showed his worth on the field, with the receiver making three catches from his four targets inside the first half. Having narrowly avoided a suspension following his actions last week against the Philadelphia Eagles, Metcalf has said a lot without even opening his mouth when it comes to the feud between his head coach and now-former quarterback. item.title: Neemias Queta on importance of center play for Boston Celtics, NBA
item.description: According to Boston Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla, the center position is the most important on any team in the NBA right now, and Boston big man Neemias Queta is inclined to agree. "I'm a center, so I'm a little bit biased, but the amount of responsibility that you have, the most efficient shots are at the rim," said ( via CLNS Media) the Portuguese center when asked about Mazzulla making such a claim in a recent Boston press conference. Noting how much pla on both ends of the court goes through big men in the NBA of today, Queta highlighted "being able to create as many easy looks at the rim offensively, whether it's through screening" as being critical. "Whether it's me getting the the dump downs, whether it's being able to being able to be a offensive rebounding guy and make make those shots, and then defensively deterring people from getting out there." "I think that impacts a lot of the game because everything else is tough shots, and we can we can play easier defense," added the Boston big man, who sees his success at center last season as more of a baseline than something to replicate. "This year is a new new season," he explained. "Whatever I did last year doesn't even matter anymore, so I'm just trying to build off of this season and keeping on growing off of the previous game." "But if I can have this year be like last year's ceiling, be my this year's floor, I think I'm in a good spot. And I think that's that's where I'm trying to get to and (continue) building off of that." Listen to "Airing Boston Celtics grievances, and feats of strength to fix them" on Spreaker. item.title: Liverpool receive huge injury boost ahead of Everton clash
item.description: Liverpool receive huge injury boost ahead of Everton clash Liverpool Injury Update: Victor Munoz Boost Ahead of Everton Clash Liverpool have one less problem than they feared ahead of the Merseyside derby. Victor Munoz, forced off in the 3-0 win over Club Brugge, has avoided serious injury. That matters, because Liverpool are already short of options and Andoni Iraola is still likely to be without Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch against Everton. Munoz went down after a heavy challenge at the end of a strong run in midweek. It looked awkward, enough to raise concerns about his knee, and enough for him to leave the pitch before half-time. The early signs, however, are positive. Iraola delivered the update in clear terms: “With Victor, I think the good news is that after assessing him, there is no disruption in the knee, everything is fine. But he has a big knock. It’s a big knock.” That does not guarantee availability for Sunday, but it changes the picture. A ligament issue would have meant weeks or months. A bruise means a late call. Iraola added: “He hasn’t trained today but he wants to try tomorrow. We’ll see how the bruise is. But I cannot tell you right now.” Liverpool would rather have Munoz than gamble unnecessarily, particularly in a derby where physical pressure is guaranteed from the first whistle. Photo: IMAGO Cody Gakpo absence remains clear There is less ambiguity with Gakpo. He will miss out, full stop. The forward has a calf problem picked up on international duty with the Netherlands and this will be his third consecutive missed match. Iraola was direct: “Cody definitely not [available against Everton]. It’s a muscle injury so we have to wait a little bit until the process goes on and it heals.” The timescale sounds ordinary enough, but muscle injuries rarely care for neat schedules. Iraola said: “This kind of injury is normally two or three weeks. He did it in the last [Netherlands] game against Germany, so normally it’s this timeline. But normally I don’t like to say timelines with injuries because every injury is different and some of them go quicker than others. It wasn’t a big injury but there is something there and you have to give the time to heal.” Ryan Gravenberch still struggling with heel pain Gravenberch is the more frustrating case. Heel pain sounds minor until it lingers for a month, which is exactly what has happened. He has not featured since the Carabao Cup last-16 win over Chelsea and there is still no clean return date. Iraola admitted: “It’s going to be difficult. I cannot say no because these kinds of injuries are difficult.” He explained the problem properly: “They don’t look like a big thing but you have the pain, it doesn’t go. Sometimes it’s better, you don’t know why. The next day, you come and it’s worse. He is dealing with this situation, we are trying to help him. The important thing is when he comes back he comes with no pain so he can play as free as possible.” Everton test arrives with squad balance i

item.title: What the Warriors are now privately saying about Draymond Green
item.description: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images The Golden State Warriors face a tough decision when it comes to Draymond Green’s future. Draymond Green is putting up 3.6 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 6.3 assists in the 2026-27 regular season for Golden State. His passing still moves the rock, but his discipline and decision-making have hurt the team, including a flagrant foul against San Antonio and a recent back-and-forth with Eddie Johnson after Johnson questioned his value and Hall of Fame case. With offense already hard to come by for the Warriors, critics keep asking what else he adds on the floor. Golden State Warriors open to trading Draymond Green Sam Amick, who was speaking on Sactown , says the Warriors still appreciate everything Draymond Green has done for the franchise, though they’re open to moving him if the right trade comes up. He said: “I’ve said before yes, and it’s always like you feel like you’re breaking Warriors code if you say that, but yes. “Yeah, absolutely. They’re not telling the GM on the other phone not to bring Draymond into the conversation.” Green is on an expiring deal, which makes his salary easy to move in a bigger package. Even after four rings together, other teams can bring him up without Golden State hanging up right away. He still has plenty of playoff savvy and defensive bite, but the Warriors are already short on points and he gives them next to nothing as a scorer. When buckets are that hard to come by, having a guy who doesn’t score on the floor makes things even tougher. item.title: Spurs guard Stephon Castle in elite company as stat sheet-stuffing star
item.description: San Antonio Spurs Stephon Castle, left) of the San Antonio Spurs is greeted by Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum at the end of the game on on Saturday, March 29, 2025 at the Frost Bank Center. (Ronald Cortes/2025 Ronald Cortes) Spurs coach Mitch Johnson heaped praise recently on Stephon Castle for his stat sheet-stuffing skill set. "He's just a Swiss army knife in the best way," Johnson said. In the aftermath of Castle's 20-point, nine-assist, six-rebound outing in Wednesday night's 116-111 loss at Portland , Spurs director of basketball communications Jordan Howenstine unearthed a fact that reinforces the coach's description of Castle's do-it-all game. The 2024-2025 NBA Rookie of the Year entered Friday night's home game against the Los Angeles Lakers as one of only three players in the league with 300 points, 100 rebounds, 100 assists and 40-plus threes this season. The others are the Lakers' Luka Doncic and Boston's Jayson Tatum, who will lead the Celtics into the Frost Bank Center for an afternoon game against the Spurs on Sunday. "The biggest thing is just keeping the versatility in my game, not trying to hone into one skill but try and be elite in a lot of different ones," Castle said after shootaround Friday afternoon. "But, yeah, it's definitely a big deal to be in the same conversation as those two guys." MORE SPURS: Carter Bryant staying thankful despite battling sophomore slump to start season Over his last four games, Castle is averaging 22.0 points, 9.5 assists, 5.8 rebounds and 1.0 steals while shooting 50% (13 of 26) from 3-point range on 6.5 attempts per game. In addition, the 22-year-old native of Covington, Ga., ranks as the Spurs' top perimeter defender. To that end, he entered Friday's game with plenty of experience defending Doncic, an assignment he will also draw when the Spurs face the Lakers on Dec. 13 in San Antonio and on Feb. 2 and April 2 in L.A. "The biggest thing is discipline," Castle said when asked what it takes to slow down the two-time NBA scoring champ from Slovenia. "He plays at his own pace. It's hard to speed him up. So when he gets to certain spots on the floor, if you're not disciplined, that's where he really hurts you. "But it's also not a one-on-one thing. We got to play great team defense. When we've had success against him in the past, we've done that." San Antonio Spurs guard Stephon Castle (5) guards Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) under the net during the third quarter at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Wednesday, Jan. 7, 2026. The Spurs love the second-round pick's shooting skills, but Castle is also impressed with his maturity. "On and off the court, he's really mature," Castle said of the 22-year-old Tennessee-ex who has split time this season between the G League Austin Spurs and the big club . item.title: Füllkrug scores late to rescue Bremen draw against Gladbach
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Werder Bremen's Niclas Füllkrug celebrates scoring his side's fourth goal during the German Bundesliga soccer match between Werder Bremen and Hamburger SV at the Weserstadion. (is associated with: «Füllkrug scores late to rescue Bremen draw against Gladbach») Carmen Jaspersen/dpa Niclas Füllkrug scored in stoppage time to rescue Werder Bremen a point in a 3-3 Bundesliga draw against last-placed Borussia Mönchengladbach on Friday. The hosts recovered from a 3-1 deficit in what was set to be a shocking defeat to Gladbach. Kevin Diks scored Gladbach's opener from the spot in the 27th minute after a handball by Youri Regeer. Eren Dinkci equalized for Bremen in the 38th, but the guests retook the lead right after the break as Honorat completed a composed finish in the 46th. The French midfielder added a second to his name in the 78th, completing a fulminant counterattack with a stunning curler from the edge of the box. It looked like Gladbach was taking all three points until Dinkci also got himself a brace in the 85th and league's top scorer Füllkrug took advantage of a defensive mistake to equalize in the second minute of stoppage time. Ahead of the weekend's matches, Bremen remain sixth, in the qualification spot for the Conference League, while Gladbach are bottom of the table with just one win in 11 matches. "Gladbach aren't exactly where they should be in the standings. When you watch the last few games, it's been tight. Today they did well, they caused us problems," Füllkrug told broadcaster Sky. "We were careless in the way we played. We have to play a clean football, we have to bring in quality." The weekend's schedule includes Hamburg v Bayern Munich on Saturday and leaders Borussia Dortmund v Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday.

item.title: Here's the matchup for (final?) MAC championship game at Ford Field
item.description: DETROIT — Say this much for the Mid-American Conference. It's got this parity thing down pat, at least in football. For the 14th consecutive year, there will be no repeat champion in football. Buffalo and Toledo punched their tickets to the MAC championship game with wins in their regular-season finales, Friday, Nov. 27. They will meet in the championship game Saturday, Dec. 5, at Ford Field in Detroit . Kickoff is at noon. Buffalo (9-3, 7-1) beat Akron, 17-9, on Friday, Nov. 27, while Toledo (10-2, 7-2) beat Ohio, 34-31. Buffalo is in the MAC championship game in Pete Lembo's second season as head coach, while Toledo is in the championship game in Mike Jacobs' first season as head coach. Their wins eliminated defending champion Western Michigan (8-4, 6-2) from contention. The Broncos won their fourth MAC championship in 2025, but lost their regular-season finale to Miami (Ohio), 28-24, in Kalamazoo earlier this week, and had to wait until Friday's games to see their fate. Five teams entered Friday still in contention to play in the MAC championship game, including Ohio and Miami (Ohio). Western Michigan beat Miami in last year's championship game , 23-13. The last team to repeat as MAC champion was Northern Illinois, which won in 2011 and 2012. If Buffalo beats Toledo next Saturday, the MAC championship will see a seventh different winner in the last seven years. Buffalo last won a MAC championship in 2008, while Toledo last won in 2022. Western Michigan, meanwhile, now awaits its bowl destination, while buzz continues to swirl around the future of fourth-year head coach Lance Taylor, who is in the mix for the opening at Maryland . One other Michigan Group of Six team has a chance to make a bowl game. That's Central Michigan (5-6, 3-4), which needs a victory Saturday, Nov. 28, on the road at Ball State to play in a bowl for the second time in as many seasons under head coach Matt Drinkall. Central Michigan lost to Northwestern, 34-7 , in last year's GameAbove Sports Bowl, which was discontinued after that game . Eastern Michigan's season is finished. At 5-7, 4-4, the Eagles missed a bowl game for the third straight year, and it led to the dismissal of head coach Chris Creighton after 13 seasons . EMU has never played in the MAC championship game, which might be coming to an end following next week's game. With the College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams next season, the Power Four conference championship games are finished after 2026. The MAC hasn't yet made a decision on whether to continue playing its championship game, which has been held at Ford Field since 2004. The MAC, notably, was the one FBS college football conference to publicly push back against CFP expansion, which doesn't guarantee more than the one spot the Group of Six already receives in the 12-team CFP format. item.title: (Video): Emegha’s quick reactions and well-timed run give Chelsea a chance
item.description: (Video): Emegha’s quick reactions and well-timed run give Chelsea a chance Emmanuel Emegha has given Chelsea their only positive moment from another defeat with a goal against Nottingham Forest. If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. Chelsea have got a goal back against Nottingham Forest. Emmanuel Emegha came on at half time and has made a difference already. He was sniffing around for a ball to drop, and when Pedro Neto’s shot hit a defender the Dutchman had his chance. He stayed onside and reacted quickly to put the ball into the net. There was a long VAR check – but the summer signing had successfully stayed on the right side of the offside line. You can see Emegha’s strike in the clip embedded here: [Footage from Sky Sports] Alonso’s Emegha call is puzzling again Emmanuel Emegha. (Photo by Gareth Copley/Getty Images) The real question is why Emegha didn’t start the game. Most fans were expecting that – he scored a goal last week and his speed allows him to affect the game far more than the lumbering Welbeck, who is seemingly only useful when your team is dominating the game in the opposition’s box. Perhaps Emegha is not yet fit for 90 minutes. But in that case he should have started and come off later. It was one of a number of puzzling lineup decisions from the manager tonight. In other news… Wesley Fofana was taken off in the second half after picking up a yellow for two dreadful compounding errors. Chelsea’s stats from the first half against Forest were truly awful – although you only had to watch the game to know how bad it was. Xabi Alonso spoke about his team selection for tonight, and it’s pretty clear what he’s aiming for from what he’s said.

item.title: Brock Purdy update doesn't bode well for 49ers to have him for Seahawks game
item.description: Brock Purdy update doesn't bode well for 49ers to have him for Seahawks game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers , coming off a dominant 35-10 victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday Night Football in Week 11, are facing a big challenge in Week 12. Going up against their NFC West division rival Seattle Seahawks , the 49ers are not going to have an easy matchup on their hands. Colton McKivitz, their starting right tackle, is done for the year. Unfortunately, he might not be the only injury this team is dealing with. As Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports, quarterback Brock Purdy wasn't at practice Friday, which doesn't bode well for his odds of suiting up against the Seahawks. Brock Purdy's odds to play vs. Seahawks in Week 12 aren't looking good "No Brock Purdy sightings early on in Friday's practice," Barrows reports. "He did not practice Wednesday and Thursday." This is not the kind of report that the 49ers fanbase will like to hear. Purdy, their MVP candidate this season, is looking to be very questionable to play this week. Purdy is dealing with an ankle injury right now, and he was a non-participant at both Wednesday's and Thursday's practices. Seeing Purdy at practice on Friday would've calmed the fears of the 49ers about not having Purdy in Week 12 against a challenging Seahawks defense. While Mac Jones is capable of playing well in a backup role, as he did last year, there's a big difference between a competent backup like Jones and an MVP candidate like Purdy. MORE : Solving the Brian Flores puzzle: How Kyle Shanahan finally bested defensive guru in 49ers win After Purdy didn't show up at Friday's practice, at least at the beginning of practice, the odds of Purdy suiting up in Week 12 against the Seahawks aren't looking good. This season, Purdy has 2,624 passing yards and 23 touchdowns to just five interceptions. In his last game against the Seahawks, he went 19 of 29 for 189 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in a win. At 10-1, the 49ers are in great shape to make the playoffs. Resting Purdy for a week would make sense, as the 49ers need to think about the playoffs now with their strong record. While winning the No. 1 seed and the NFC West are important things to consider, there's still a lot of season left. A loss to the Seahawks in Week 12 wouldn't be the end of the world. Besides, Jones could win this game, and it wouldn't be a huge surprise. Purdy hasn't shown up to practice this week for the 49ers, and his odds of playing in Week 12 aren't looking good. Based on this report from Barrows, 49ers fans might have to realize that Purdy might really miss this week as he deals with an ankle injury. item.title: LeBron James Triple-Double Lifts Sixers Past Heat On Wednesday
item.description: Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James proved he can carry the Philadelphia 76ers even when their best player sits out. On Wednesday night, James recorded his first triple-double in a Sixers uniform, posting 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds to lead the team to a 111-104 victory over the Miami Heat. The win moves the Sixers to a 15-4 record on the season and keeps their NBA Cup dreams alive, according to Sports Illustrated . This performance shows that Philadelphia does not need to rely solely on Joel Embiid to win games. The team faced a tough test with Embiid ruled out due to illness. James stepped up immediately, scoring 14 consecutive points in the second quarter. With 16 points, 6 rebounds, and 6 assists, he closed out the first half. In the opening half, he made all three of his long-range shots, showing hot form. This offensive flow allowed the Sixers to control the pace against a Miami team that had won seven games in a row. Maxey Delivers When It Counts Tyrese Maxey provided the extra scoring punch the team desperately needed. With Jaylen Brown sidelined for the second half due to a hamstring injury, Maxey took over. The game ended with him scoring a team-high 30 points, plus four rebounds and six assists. According to The Lufkin Daily News , this was Maxey’s third 30-point game of the season. He was efficient on offense, hitting 12 of his 21 field goal attempts. His ability to create his own shot was vital in a game where the Sixers were short-handed. James also hit 50 percent or better from the floor in four straight contests. He is finding his rhythm quickly with this new team. The combination of James and Maxey created a scoring threat that Miami could not stop. Even without Embiid, the Sixers found a way to win a close contest. The 111-104 final score reflects how tight the game was, but the result was clear. Heat Streak Snapped in Philadelphia The loss ended Miami’s seven-game winning streak. Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Heat with 32 points and 14 rebounds, but it was not enough. Davion Mitchell tallied 20 points alongside 10 assists, whereas Bam Adebayo notched 17 points and 11 rebounds. The Heat now sit at 2-1 in NBA Cup play, just like the Sixers. Both teams have one game remaining in their group. The Miami Heat face New York, the defending NBA Cup champion, in Friday night’s Group B final. The Sixers will look to build on this momentum as they continue their push for the title.

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino warns Man Utd players 'I'm not nice' as he calls for mentality change
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino has yet to win since taking charge of Manchester United -Credit:Zohaib Alam, Manchester United via Getty Images Mauricio Pochettino acknowledged he had observed encouraging signs during his opening two matches as Manchester United manager, though he also cautioned his squad that he is "not nice." Pochettino suffered defeat in his debut fixture against Liverpool at Anfield last weekend, before his side salvaged a 2-2 draw with Sporting Lisbon in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday. The 54-year-old has had just one day at Carrington to ready his team for Brentford, as the squad returned to Manchester on Thursday following a recovery session in Portugal, and it was suggested to Pochettino during his media briefing that he's navigated a whirlwind opening eight days at United. -Credit:Zohaib Alam, Manchester United via Getty Images Addressing that observation, Pochettino stated he had witnessed positive elements from his players but emphasized that he is "not nice," according to the Manchester Evening News . item.title: Raiders’ Jackson Powers-Johnson suffers potentially serious injury at practice
item.description: An already-frustrating season for Raiders offensive lineman Jackson Powers-Johnson took an ominous turn Friday when he suffered a potentially serious injury during practice. Powers-Johnson was ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Browns and could be sidelined considerably longer. “He had an injury at practice today, and we’ll have more details for you tomorrow,” Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Friday. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) celebrates a touchdown with Jackson Powers-Johnson (58) and Connor Heyward (34) in Las Vegas, Nov. 15, 2026. AP Photo/David Becker Asked if the injury was serious, Kubiak acknowledged the possibility. “Could be, yes,” Kubiak said. “We’ll go take a peek at him here after this and have more info for you.” It’s the latest setback for a player whose first three NFL seasons have fallen short of the lofty expectations that accompanied his arrival in Las Vegas. Jackson Powers-Johnson of the Las Vegas Raiders arrives at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, for a game against the Seattle Seahawks. Getty Images The Raiders selected Powers-Johnson with the 44th overall pick in the second round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Oregon, where he won the Rimington Trophy as college football’s best center. The expectation was that Powers-Johnson would become a foundational piece along the Raiders’ offensive line, either at center or guard. Instead, injuries and an inability to establish himself as a permanent starter have prevented that from materializing. Powers-Johnson started 14 games as a rookie, splitting time between left guard and center. His second season was cut short by an ankle injury. Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak speaks during a news conference after an NFL football game in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/David Zalubowski The offseason signing of Tyler Linderbaum effectively closed the door on Powers-Johnson becoming the Raiders’ long-term answer at center. And he has been unable to maintain a firm grip on the starting right guard job. Now, depending on the severity of Friday’s injury, Powers-Johnson could face yet another obstacle in his effort to establish himself as part of the Raiders’ future, with next season representing the final year of his rookie contract.

item.title: Serie A | Venezia 0-0 Bologna: Stanković and Skorupski stand firm in stalemate
item.description: Serie A | Venezia 0-0 Bologna: Stanković and Skorupski stand firm in stalemate Filip Stanković and Łukasz Skorupski were the stars at the Penzo as bottom-of-the-table Venezia held Bologna to a goalless draw, with Redouane Halhal having an early opener ruled out by VAR. Venezia came into the game bottom of Serie A with six points from 12 games, after a 4-0 thrashing at Juventus on Sunday. Davide Nicola was without the injured Franjić, Šverko and Thierry Correia, but handed a start to Gianluca Busio in midfield. Bologna, ninth on 18 points, had drawn 1-1 with Udinese last week . Raffaele Palladino left Riccardo Orsolini and Artem Dovbyk on the bench, while Lorenzo De Silvestri, Emil Holm, Juan Miranda, Oussama El Azzouzi and Ukko Happonen were all injured. Venezia made the brighter start, and Skorupski had to dive low to his right to keep out John Yeboah’s effort after a defence-splitting pass from Akor Adams. The hosts thought they had taken the lead in the 14th minute. Halhal burst into the box to meet Antoine Hainaut’s whipped cross and finish into the bottom corner. However, the goal was ruled out for offside after a lengthy VAR check. Tempers flared in the aftermath, with Juan Jesus and Nadir Zortea both booked for dissent, and Martin Vitík and Hainaut soon joined them in the book. Skorupski was the busier goalkeeper in the first half. He produced a sharp save to deny Kike Pérez’s low volley on the half-hour, then thwarted Yeboah again from inside the box shortly before the break. At the other end, Jens Odgaard fired over from a good position and Arthur Theate headed straight at Stanković. Bologna improved after the restart, with Matteo Darmian on for Vitík. Stanković pulled off a superb reflex save to keep out Nicolò Casale’s header, and Federico Bernardeschi curled just wide from a set piece moments later. VENICE, ITALY – NOVEMBER 27: Riccardo Orsolini of Bologna FC during the Serie A match between Venezia FC and Bologna FC at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo on November 27, 2026 in Venice, Italy. (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images) Venezia 0-0 Bologna: Juan Jesus hits the post in dramatic second half Palladino turned to Orsolini and Nicolò Cambiaghi just before the hour, while Nicola sent on Thórir Jóhann Helgason for Busio. Helgason almost had an immediate impact. His set-piece delivery found Juan Jesus, whose header from the edge of the six-yard box came back off the post. Bologna brought on Roberto Piccoli for Odgaard, and he blazed over from Rahim Alhassane’s cross. Venezia refreshed their attack with Albion Rrahmani and Lion Lauberbach, and the latter forced a strong save from Skorupski at his near post. The chances kept coming in the closing stages. Stanković denied Lewis Ferguson’s header and then made his best save of the night to stop Tommaso Pobega from inside the six-yard box. Skorupski rushed out to smother Helgason’s effort at the other end, and Alhassane fired high and wide. Venezia 0-0 Bologna

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
